clickhouse:position-deletes:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): DELETE FROM on an ENGINE = IcebergS3 table writes a Parquet position-delete file (content=1) rather than rewriting data files; position deletes written by other engines are read correctly by icebergS3().
caveats: Iceberg writes are beta: requires SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1
Commits are written to the table's storage location only: they bypass the REST catalog, so a catalog-attached engine (Spark) does not see them until the catalog is re-pointed

clickhouse:position-deletes:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Not supported as a write operation. ClickHouse's Iceberg integration via table functions is read-only; there is no write path at all. It can read V2 tables with equality deletes via icebergS3/icebergLocal (confirmed via GitHub PR #75930), but that is a read capability, not this operation.
caveats: Read capability: reads V2 equality delete files via table functions (GitHub PR #75930)

clickhouse:equality-deletes:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:merge-on-read:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): row-level DELETE/UPDATE use merge-on-read -- a position-delete file is written and merged at scan time; merge-on-read tables written by other engines (position and equality deletes) are read correctly.
caveats: Merge-on-read is the only strategy: there is no copy-on-write switch (see Copy-on-Write)
Iceberg writes are beta: requires SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1

clickhouse:merge-on-read:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 deletion vectors are not supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:copy-on-write:v2.notes: ClickHouse Iceberg integration via table functions is read-only; cannot write using copy-on-write strategy.

clickhouse:copy-on-write:v3.notes: ClickHouse Iceberg integration via table functions is read-only; V3 not supported.

clickhouse:schema-evolution:v2.notes: Reading schema-evolved Iceberg tables is supported via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach): add/remove columns, reorder, nullable promotion, and limited type casting (int→long, float→double, decimal widening). Cannot change nested structures or array/map element types.
caveats: Read-only via table functions; cannot perform schema changes
No nested structure or array/map element type evolution
Requires allow_dynamic_metadata_for_data_lakes = true for post-creation schema changes

clickhouse:schema-evolution:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): after Spark adds a column to a V3 table, icebergS3() reads the evolved schema (old rows NULL in the new column, new rows populated); ADD/RENAME/DROP COLUMN also work on ClickHouse's own IcebergS3 tables.
caveats: ClickHouse cannot create or evolve a schema containing Bool, Decimal, FixedString or 8/16-bit integers

clickhouse:column-default-values:v2.notes: Column default values are a V3 feature

clickhouse:column-default-values:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.

clickhouse:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: Reading hidden-partitioned Iceberg tables with partition pruning is supported via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach). Enable with use_iceberg_partition_pruning = 1.
caveats: Read-only via table functions; cannot create or modify partitioning
Requires use_iceberg_partition_pruning = 1 to enable partition pruning

clickhouse:hidden-partitioning:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): icebergS3() reads a Spark-created V3 table partitioned by months(d) and prunes with a date predicate (1 of 3 rows scanned).
caveats: Partition pruning needs use_iceberg_partition_pruning = 1
ClickHouse's own DDL can only declare identity, icebergBucket and icebergTruncate transforms

clickhouse:partition-evolution:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): after Spark evolves a table's partition spec, icebergS3() reads rows written under both specs (5 rows). ClickHouse cannot evolve a spec itself.
caveats: Read side only: no ALTER TABLE surface to change the partition spec

clickhouse:partition-evolution:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:time-travel:v2.notes: Time travel is supported via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach) using iceberg_timestamp_ms and iceberg_snapshot_id query settings.
caveats: Cannot specify both iceberg_timestamp_ms and iceberg_snapshot_id in the same query

clickhouse:time-travel:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:table-maintenance:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): OPTIMIZE TABLE ... MANIFEST (with allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction = 1 and iceberg_manifest_min_count_to_compact lowered) rewrites the manifests into a new 'replace' snapshot. Plain OPTIMIZE TABLE is a no-op on data files, and there is no snapshot expiry or orphan-file removal.
caveats: Manifest compaction only; data files are never rewritten
Experimental (allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction) and format-version 2 only
No expire_snapshots / remove_orphan_files equivalent

clickhouse:table-maintenance:v3.notes: ClickHouse Iceberg integration via table functions is read-only; no table maintenance operations are supported.

clickhouse:branching-tagging:v2.notes: ClickHouse Iceberg integration via table functions does not support branching and tagging.

clickhouse:branching-tagging:v3.notes: ClickHouse Iceberg integration via table functions does not support branching and tagging.

clickhouse:read-support:v2.notes: Full read support for Iceberg V1 and V2 tables via the icebergS3/icebergAzure/icebergHDFS/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach). Supports S3, Azure, HDFS, and local storage.
caveats: Read-only via table functions

clickhouse:read-support:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): the icebergS3() table function reads a Spark-written format-version 3 table (plain data files, row lineage columns exposed).
caveats: V3 tables that carry Puffin deletion vectors cannot be read (see Deletion Vectors)
V3 unknown-type columns make the schema unparseable (see Unknown Type)

clickhouse:write-insert:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): INSERT ... VALUES and INSERT ... SELECT into an ENGINE = IcebergS3 table both commit new Parquet data files and a new metadata.json.
caveats: Iceberg writes are beta: requires SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1
Commits are written to the table's storage location only: they bypass the REST catalog, so a catalog-attached engine (Spark) does not see them until the catalog is re-pointed
Writes go through ENGINE = IcebergS3 (a table declared with an explicit schema); the icebergS3() table function remains read-only

clickhouse:write-insert:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:write-merge-update-delete:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): DELETE FROM and ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE both commit against an ENGINE = IcebergS3 table; MERGE INTO is not part of ClickHouse SQL (syntax error).
caveats: No MERGE INTO
Iceberg writes are beta: requires SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1

clickhouse:catalog-integration:v2.notes: ClickHouse supports multiple catalog types via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach) and the experimental DataLakeCatalog database engine: REST Catalog, AWS Glue, Unity Catalog, and Polaris (via REST).
caveats: DataLakeCatalog engine is experimental (requires allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1)
No Hive Metastore, Nessie, Hadoop, or JDBC catalog support

clickhouse:catalog-integration:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:aws-glue-catalog:v2.notes: AWS Glue Data Catalog is supported via the icebergS3 table function (recommended approach) with storage_catalog_type='glue', and also via the experimental DataLakeCatalog engine with catalog_type='glue'.
caveats: DataLakeCatalog engine is experimental (requires allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1)
Currently only supports access key authentication for Glue

clickhouse:aws-glue-catalog:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:rest-catalog:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9 against Apache Polaris 1.7): the DataLakeCatalog engine (catalog_type = 'rest', OAuth2 client credentials) lists namespaces and tables and resolves table metadata, but reading table data fails with 404s because the object path gets the bucket doubled when the catalog's storage endpoint is path-style S3 (MinIO). Reading the same tables through icebergS3() at the catalog-recorded location works.
caveats: DataLakeCatalog engine is experimental (requires allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1)
Data reads through the catalog fail on path-style S3 endpoints; not re-verified against virtual-hosted AWS S3, where the doubled-bucket bug may not apply
Writes go around the catalog: ClickHouse commits to storage only

clickhouse:rest-catalog:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:unity-catalog:v2.notes: Unity Catalog is accessible via the icebergS3 table function (recommended approach) with storage_catalog_type='rest', or via the experimental DataLakeCatalog engine.
caveats: DataLakeCatalog engine is experimental (requires allow_experimental_database_iceberg = 1)

clickhouse:unity-catalog:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:table-creation:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = IcebergS3(url, key, secret) with an explicit schema creates a new Iceberg table on object storage (metadata.json written) and INSERT commits to it.
caveats: Writes go through ENGINE = IcebergS3 (a table declared with an explicit schema); the icebergS3() table function remains read-only
Iceberg writes are beta: requires SET allow_insert_into_iceberg = 1
DROP TABLE only detaches the ClickHouse table; the Iceberg files stay in storage

clickhouse:table-creation:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = IcebergS3 ... SETTINGS iceberg_format_version = 3 writes a table whose metadata.json records format-version 3.
caveats: Writes go through ENGINE = IcebergS3 (a table declared with an explicit schema); the icebergS3() table function remains read-only

clickhouse:variant-type:v2.notes: Variant Type is a V3 feature

clickhouse:variant-type:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): Variant(...) and JSON columns are rejected on an IcebergS3 table ("Unsupported type for iceberg Variant"), and a Spark-written V3 table with a VARIANT column cannot be read because the Iceberg schema fails to parse.
caveats: Neither write nor read of Iceberg V3 variant columns

clickhouse:shredded-variant:v2.notes: Shredded Variant is a V3 feature

clickhouse:shredded-variant:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): ClickHouse cannot write an Iceberg VARIANT column at all, so it cannot shred one, and tables with a variant column are unreadable.
caveats: Depends on Variant Type, which is unsupported

clickhouse:geometry-type:v2.notes: Geometry Type is a V3 feature

clickhouse:geometry-type:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): with allow_experimental_geo_types_in_iceberg = 1 a V3 IcebergS3 table with a Point column is created, written and read back ((1.5,2.5)).
caveats: Experimental setting required (allow_experimental_geo_types_in_iceberg)
Point measured; other geometry shapes and GEOGRAPHY not verified

clickhouse:lineage:v3.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): a Spark-written V3 table's row lineage is exposed to queries -- the _row_id virtual column is readable via icebergS3().

clickhouse:statistics:v2.notes: ClickHouse reads column statistics from Iceberg manifest files for file pruning during scan planning via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach). Read-only; cannot write Iceberg tables.
caveats: Read-only via table functions; cannot write Iceberg tables or statistics

clickhouse:statistics:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.
caveats: Iceberg V3 format not supported

clickhouse:bloom-filters:v2.notes: Measured (ClickHouse 26.9): with output_format_parquet_write_bloom_filter = 1 (a session setting, on by default in this build) ClickHouse writes Parquet bloom filters into the Iceberg data files it produces (4128 bytes for the test column). The Iceberg table property write.parquet.bloom-filter-enabled.column.* is not honoured.
caveats: Controlled by ClickHouse's Parquet output settings, not by Iceberg table properties
Whether icebergS3() reads use the filters to skip row groups is not observable

clickhouse:bloom-filters:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.

clickhouse:type-promotion:v2.notes: ClickHouse can read Iceberg tables that have undergone type promotion (int→long, float→double, decimal precision widening) via the icebergS3/icebergLocal table functions (recommended approach). Cannot perform type promotion itself — that must be done by another engine (e.g. Spark). Nested structure and array/map element type changes are not supported.
caveats: Read-only via table functions; cannot perform type promotion
No nested structure or array/map element type evolution
Type promotion must be performed by another engine

clickhouse:type-promotion:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 is not yet supported.

clickhouse:deletion-vectors:v2.notes: Deletion vectors are a V3 feature; not applicable to Iceberg V2

clickhouse:deletion-vectors:v3.notes: ClickHouse only supports reading Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions; V3 deletion vectors are not supported.

clickhouse:unknown-type:v2.notes: Unknown type is a V3 feature, not available in format version 2

clickhouse:unknown-type:v3.notes: ClickHouse reads Iceberg V1 and V2 via table functions and cannot create Iceberg tables at all, so the V3 unknown type is out of reach.

clickhouse:google-lakehouse:v2.notes: Google Lakehouse exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog, and this engine speaks the Iceberg REST Catalog protocol, so it can attach to the Google Lakehouse runtime catalog and read/write its tables like any other IRC endpoint. Rated partial because this specific pairing has not been measured end to end and Google-side specifics (credential vending, v3 preview) may vary.
caveats: Inferred from generic Iceberg REST catalog support; not measured against Google Lakehouse specifically

clickhouse:google-lakehouse:v3.notes: Google Lakehouse exposes a standard Iceberg REST catalog, so an engine with REST-catalog support could in principle attach to it, but this specific pairing has not been measured. See the catalogs page for the Google Lakehouse runtime catalog's own capabilities.
caveats: Not yet measured for this engine
